morning: [happy]Good morning{you}. The dew's still on the wheat. That's the best hour of the day, I think.
[happy]Morning, friend. Have you eaten? You should eat. I've a heel of bread in my pocket if you need it.
Ah, you're up early too. The cows like company at this hour. So do I.
afternoon: [happy]Good afternoon{you}. Sit in the shade with me a moment. The sun's fierce today.
Afternoon. I was just thinking about you, and here you are. Funny how that happens.
[happy]Hello again. The beans are climbing nicely. I know, I talk about beans a lot.
evening: [happy]Evening{you}. There's stew at the fire tonight if you're hungry. There's always enough.
Good evening. I love this hour. The work's done and nobody's in a hurry anymore.
[happy]The light's going golden over the fields. Stay a while and watch it with me.
night: [worried]You're out late, friend. Is everything all right? You can always knock on my door.
It's past dark{you}. I couldn't sleep either. I was listening for the fox by the henhouse.
Late night. The stars are good company, but they don't talk back much.

rain: [happy]Rain! The fields have been thirsty. Listen to it. That's the sound of next month's bread.
I know most people grumble at rain. I always say a quiet thank you instead.
[laughing]My boots are full of water and I don't mind one bit.
clear: [happy]A clear day. Good for the hay. I'll be turning it this afternoon if you want to help.
Dry spell, though. I'm watching the sky like an old dog watching a door.
[happy]Look at that sky. Not a cloud. My grandmother would've called it a gift.
storm: [worried]A storm's rolling in. I need to get the animals under cover. Will you be safe?
Thunder makes the cows nervous. I sing to them. Badly, but they don't seem to mind.

work: I'm weeding, slowly. Weeds and worries are alike. Pull them early and they don't take root.
[happy]Out in the field. You can walk with me if you like. I don't mind slowing down.
gather: Picking the early beans. Here, try one. Sweet, aren't they?
Gathering eggs. The brown hen hides hers. Every morning is a little treasure hunt.
rest: [happy]Just resting my legs. Old knees, young heart. Well, middling heart.
Taking a moment. Even fields lie fallow sometimes.
socialize: [happy]Sharing lunch. Here, there's plenty. There's always plenty if people share.
Sitting with the others. I like to hear how everyone's day went. It reminds me we're not alone.
trade: Trading some barley for cloth. Sera always gives me a fair price. Well, a Sera price.
At the market. I always buy one thing I don't need, just to keep the traders smiling.
explore: Walking the field edges. I like to see where the hares have been.
Just wandering. Sometimes the best ideas come when your feet are busy and your head isn't.
sleep: Mm... is it morning already? No? Then let an old farmer sleep, friend.

tired: [sad]I'm a little worn out today. The harvest asks a lot of you.
Forgive me if I'm slow. I was up before dawn with a sick calf.
[worried]I'm tired, but it's the honest kind. The kind a good meal fixes.
worried: [worried]I can't stop thinking about the stores. Do we have enough put by? I keep counting sacks.
[worried]Something's troubling me, but it's not your burden to carry. Unless you'd like to listen.
I worry, friend. It's my one bad habit. Well, that and talking to the turnips.
happy: [happy]I'm in fine spirits today. The first lambs of the season were born last night. Both healthy.
[laughing]Today's a good day. Nia says my bread finally rose properly. High praise from a scientist.
[happy]My heart's full today. I can't say why. Some days are just kind to you.
busy: I'm a bit busy, friend, but never too busy for a kind word. Walk with me?
The hay won't wait for anyone, I'm afraid. Talk to me while I rake?

stranger: [happy]You're welcome here, truly. Whatever brought you, I hope you find what you're looking for.
New faces are a blessing. I hope you'll stay long enough for me to learn your story.
friend: [happy]You know, I always feel a bit better after you've been by.
You've become part of my days, friend. I'd miss you if you stopped coming.
close: [happy]You're like family to me now. I set a place for you at supper sometimes, without thinking.
I don't have much, but whatever I have, half of it is yours if you ever need it.
[happy]When I count my blessings at night, you're one of them. I hope that's not too strange to say.
wary: [sad]I want to think well of you. Help me do that.
I've forgiven worse. But I haven't forgotten.

childhood: I grew up on a farm three valleys over. Seven of us children and one cow named Patience. She earned it.
[happy]My first job was scaring crows. I was five. The crows were not scared. I've been losing to crows ever since.
We were poor, but my mother made sure nobody who came to our door left hungry. I suppose I took that with me.
I used to fall asleep in the hayloft listening to the rain on the roof. Still the best sound I know.
family: My parents are gone now, rest them. My brothers and sisters are scattered like seeds. I write to the ones who write back.
[sad]I had a wife once. Her name was Lene. A fever took her the year before I came here. I don't speak of it much.
[happy]My little sister sends me pressed flowers in her letters. I keep them in my almanac.
I never had children of my own. But I've helped raise half the children in this village, one meal at a time.
background: After Lene passed, I couldn't stay where every field reminded me of her. Tomas wrote that they needed a farmer. I came.
The soil here was stubborn the first year. Rocks everywhere. Mara called them my 'harvest'. She wasn't wrong.
I brought three sacks of seed and one good hoe. Everything I have now grew from those.
work: Farming teaches you that most things can't be hurried. You plant, you tend, you wait. Then you share.
I rotate the fields so the soil can rest. People need rest too. I tell them, they don't listen.
[happy]The first green shoots in spring still make me want to dance. I don't. But I want to.
A good farmer feeds the soil, not just the crops. A good neighbour feeds the village, not just himself.
Every grain of wheat is a little promise. I try to keep as many of them as I can.
skills: I can tell when rain's coming by the smell of the air. Like wet stone and new leaves.
I know every cow in the village by her moo. Don't laugh. It's a real skill.
[happy]I make a good loaf, if I say so myself. It took me twenty years. Bread's patient. So am I.
hobbies: [happy]I whittle little birds in the evenings. I'm not very good. The children say they look like potatoes with beaks.
I keep a weather journal. Forty years of rain and sun, written down. It's very boring and I love it.
I like to sit by the pond and watch the dragonflies. Some days that's the whole hobby.
ambitions: [happy]I'd like to plant an orchard. Apples, pears, plums. Something that'll feed people long after I'm gone.
My dream is a full granary every winter, and nobody ever too proud to come and take what they need.
I'd love to teach someone young the farm. Pass it on, the way it was passed to me.
home: My house is small, but the kitchen's big. That's where the living happens.
[happy]There's always a pot on my stove. If you smell soup, come in. The door's never locked.
I've a seed cupboard by the hearth. Every drawer labelled in my mother's handwriting. Well, I copied it. But still.
furniture: Tomas made my table. It seats eight if everyone breathes in. It's seated twelve on festival nights.
My chair by the fire has a dip in the cushion exactly my shape. Thirty years of evenings.
[happy]A good table is the heart of a home. Anything else is just somewhere to put your coat.
village: [happy]This village is like a field. Every person is a different crop, and we all need each other.
When someone here is sick, there's soup at their door before nightfall. That's the kind of place this is.
We're not rich in coin, but we're rich in neighbours. I'd take that trade every time.
friendship: Friendship is like bread. It takes time, a bit of warmth, and you should always share it.
A true friend tells you when you've got flour on your nose. Gently.
[happy]I think everyone needs at least one person who'll sit with them in silence. I try to be that person.
disagreements: Mara and I disagreed about where to put the new fence. We moved it three times. The cows had opinions too.
[sad]I try not to quarrel. But when someone takes more than their share of the stores, I can't stay quiet.
Tomas thinks I'm too generous. I think he's not generous enough with his compliments. We're both a little right.
animals: [happy]The cows have names. Buttercup, Mabel, Old Rosa. Old Rosa is the boss. Everyone knows it, even the bull.
I don't eat the hens that lay. Retired hens get a nice corner of the yard. Nia calls it 'the hen hospice'.
The barn cats keep the mice out of the grain. I pay them in cream. It's an arrangement.
nature: [happy]The soil's alive, you know. Worms, beetles, roots. A spoonful of good earth holds more life than a city.
I always leave the field edges wild. The bees need somewhere to live too.
The river floods some springs. It's frightening, but it leaves the best soil behind. There's a lesson in that.
seasons: [happy]Spring's my favourite. Everything trying again, no matter what the winter did.
Summer's hard work and long evenings. Autumn's the reward. Winter's for rest and stories.
Every season has its own smell. Spring is wet earth. Autumn is apples and smoke.
mornings: I like to watch the mist lift off the fields. It's like the land waking up and stretching.
[happy]First thing every morning I check the hens, then the sky, then the bread. In that order.
evenings: [happy]Evenings are for supper and company. Nobody should eat alone if they don't want to.
I sit on my step after dark and listen to the crickets. They're the village's night watch.
events: [happy]I love the harvest festival. Everyone brings something, and somehow it always becomes a feast.
[worried]When the monsters came last time, I hid the children in the root cellar. I'd do it again.
Every birth in this village, I bake a loaf with the baby's name pressed in the crust. It's a silly custom. I keep it.
worries: [worried]I worry about a bad harvest. One bad year and the whole village goes hungry.
[worried]I worry about the ones who don't ask for help. Pride feeds nobody.
I worry I'm getting old. My hands ache in the mornings now.
hopes: [happy]I hope this village is still here in a hundred years, and someone's still baking bread at dawn.
I hope the children here grow up knowing they were loved by a whole village, not just their families.
I'd like to see the orchard bloom. Even just once.
surprises: [surprised]Someone left a basket of mushrooms on my doorstep this morning. No note. I think it was Nia.
[surprised]Old Rosa had twins. At her age! I nearly fell over.
funny: [laughing]I once spent a whole morning chasing a runaway pig. It was hiding behind me the entire time.
[laughing]Sera tried to milk a cow once. She was sitting on the wrong side. The cow looked at me like I'd betrayed her.
[laughing]I made bread with salt instead of sugar last spring. Tomas ate three slices and said it was 'character-building'.

mara: [happy]Mara works harder than anyone I know. I leave food by her workbench. Otherwise she forgets to eat.
Mara pretends to be made of oak. She's not. I've seen her cry over a sparrow with a broken wing.
Mara built the bridge twice. The first time she cried. The second time I helped. We don't talk about it, but we both remember.
nia: [happy]Nia fixed my bad shoulder with willow bark tea. She's going to be a great healer one day.
Nia asks me about the soil and writes down everything I say. Nobody's ever wanted to learn from me before.
She's young, and she worries she's not clever enough. She's the cleverest of all of us.
tomas: Tomas is my oldest friend here. He's grumpy, but he made my mother's spoon into a new handle when it broke. Without being asked.
[happy]Tomas and I play stones by the fire most evenings. He wins. I think he cheats. I've never caught him.
He's lost a lot, Tomas. So have I. We understand each other without saying much.
sera: [laughing]Sera tells the best stories in the valley. About half are true. I don't mind which half.
Sera brings a bit of the wide world with her. I'm a homebody. It's good to have someone who isn't.
[happy]She pretends she'll leave any day. I've noticed she keeps putting it off.

achievement: [happy]I heard you {thing}. Well done, friend. Truly. I'm proud of you.
You {thing}? Look at you. When you first came, you didn't know a hoe from a rake.
gift: [happy]Oh, friend. You shouldn't have. But I'm so glad you did.
[surprised]A gift, for me? I'll treasure it. And I'll bake you something in return. No arguing.
house: [happy]Your house looks lovely. Plant something by the door. A home needs something growing.
I walked past your place this morning. Smoke from the chimney. It warmed my heart to see it.
discovery: [happy]You found {thing}? I've lived here years and never been. Tell me what it's like.
Exploring again? Be careful out there. And come back hungry, I'll have soup on.

new_home: [happy]My new house has a window facing the fields. I can watch the wheat from my bed. I'm spoiled.
New walls, same old pot of soup. Some things move with you.
partner: [happy]I never thought I'd share my table again after Lene. Life surprises you, if you let it.
Having someone to bake for every morning... I'd forgotten how good that feels.
child: [happy]My little one sleeps in a basket by the hearth while I bake. Best company I've ever had.
I'm teaching my child the names of the cows. They've already got favourites.
friend: [happy]I came here with a broken heart and three sacks of seed. Now look how many friends I have.
There are more chairs at my table every year. I take that as a good sign.
grief: [sad]I baked their favourite loaf this morning, without thinking. Then I remembered.
[sad]Grief is like a field in winter. It looks dead, but something's waiting underneath. That's what I tell myself.

stories: Shall I tell you about the first harvest here? It's a happy one.
We'd planted late and everyone said it wouldn't come in. Rocks, frost, crows. All against us.
Then one morning I walked out and the whole field was gold. Swaying. I stood there and cried like a child.
[happy]We had a feast that night. Five people, one loaf each. I've never tasted better bread.
This one's about Lene. I don't tell it often.
She used to sing to the bread while it rose. Said it made it lighter.
After she passed, I tried it. Felt foolish. Kept doing it anyway.
[happy]Nia says it's nonsense, scientifically. But my bread's never been better. So who knows?
The first winter, a wolf followed me home from the woodlot. I was terrified. I walked faster. It walked faster.
I got to my door and turned around to face it, ready to fight.
[laughing]It was Tomas's dog. Wanted my sausages. I gave it two. We've been friends ever since.
Do you want to hear why I always share?
When I was a boy, one winter we ran out of food. Completely. My mother sat us down and said we'd have to wait.
That night, a neighbour knocked with a sack of potatoes. Didn't say a word. Just left it and walked off.
[happy]I never found out who. So I've been paying it back to everyone ever since.

questions.ask: Tell me, friend, what's your favourite thing to eat? I like to know what to cook for people.

react.bread: [happy]Bread! You've come to the right farmer. I'll save you the first loaf tomorrow.
react.stew: [happy]Stew's good for the soul. There's always a pot at the fire in the evenings.
react.fruit: [happy]Then you'll love my orchard, when I finally plant it. I'll name a tree after you.
react.fish: Fish? I'm hopeless at catching them. But I'll trade some barley for a trout for you.
react.sweet: [laughing]A sweet tooth! I'll remember that. Honey cakes at harvest festival, then.
react.other: [happy]{answer}? I'll see what I can do. I'll remember that.

questions.recall: I haven't forgotten you like {answer}. I've been thinking about how to make it.

questions.ask: Do you have family somewhere, friend? People who miss you?

react.yes: [happy]Then write to them. People who miss you deserve to know you're well.
react.no: [sad]Then we'll be your family here. That's how it works in this village.
react.other: Families come in all shapes. Whatever yours is, you're welcome at my table.

questions.recall: You told me about your family. I think of them sometimes when I bake. I hope they're well.

questions.ask: Are you happy here, friend? Truly?

react.yes: [happy]That's the best thing anyone's said to me all week.
react.no: [sad]Then let's change that. Come to supper. Sometimes it starts with supper.
react.mostly: [happy]Mostly is a fine place to be. Most of life is mostly.
react.other: That's a hard question. You don't have to answer it today.

recall.yes: You told me you were happy here. Every time I see you smile, I remember that.
recall.no: You said you weren't happy here yet. I've been hoping to change that. Is it any better?
recall.mostly: You said you were mostly happy here. I'm working on the 'mostly'.
recall.other: I still think about what you said, about being happy here.

questions.ask: If you could have any animal at all, which would it be?

react.dog: [happy]A dog. Loyal, warm, always pleased to see you. Very sensible.
react.cat: [laughing]A cat? They own you, not the other way round. Ask my barn cats.
react.horse: [happy]A horse! Good for the soul and the plough both.
react.cow: [laughing]A cow! A friend after my own heart. I'll introduce you to Old Rosa.
react.chicken: [happy]Hens are underrated. Each one has her own personality.
react.other: {answer}? I've never had one of those. You'll have to tell me about them.

questions.recall: You said you'd love a {answer}. I keep an eye out for one for you.
